subject.title: fix(plugins): terminate git clone args so git: specs cannot inject options

question: Should OpenClaw accept this strict mitigation for dash-leading `git:` specs in plugin and skill source installs?
rationale: The code fix is narrow and well-supported, but it intentionally changes the accepted `git:` spec boundary in a security-sensitive install path.

options.title: Land the strict mitigation
options.body: Reject dash-leading specs before git runs and keep `--` at both clone call sites for defense in depth.

options.title: Preserve unusual dash-leading paths
options.body: Ask for a revised patch that keeps the `--` terminator but permits some dash-leading repository names under a documented compatibility rule.

recommendation.title: Land the strict mitigation
recommendation.body: Reject dash-leading specs before git runs and keep `--` at both clone call sites for defense in depth.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent install-policy work makes this the best available owner for reviewing the install security boundary.
